scope: whole repository -- no package named in the prompt
_meta.role: reference/fasit agent -- unlimited time/token budget, produces the ground-truth answer the other two arms are scored against; cross-checked the package graph with a second independent method, `go build ./...` at the pinned SHA, which succeeds cleanly and confirms every symbol named below is present and referenced exactly as described

key_symbols.name: configsync.ReconcileAll
key_symbols.role: Iterates configreg.Modules(), reads each module's on-disk file, and calls yamlengine.Reconcile against that module's template, writing the merged result when apply is true; skips the fabric module entirely, since it is repo-wide rather than per-worktree.

key_symbols.name: configsync.ReconcileFabricAt
key_symbols.role: The repo-wide counterpart to ReconcileAll for the one module ReconcileAll skips: reconciles the single fabric.yaml at a board directory, folding in pre-cutover legacy warp.yaml/weft.yaml values on first materialization.

key_symbols.name: configsync.legacyFabricConfig
key_symbols.role: Reads any pre-cutover warp.yaml/weft.yaml still on disk and concatenates their values so ReconcileFabricAt can migrate them into the new fabric.yaml on first run.

key_symbols.name: configreg.Modules
key_symbols.role: Returns the ordered registry of every known config module (name + template function + SeedOnly flag); this is the list configsync.ReconcileAll walks.

key_symbols.name: configreg.Module.SeedOnly
key_symbols.role: Marks a module (e.g. models, burler) whose key set is operator-owned open-ended data; ReconcileAll materializes its template only when the file is absent and never adds/removes keys from a present file, unlike the default per-key reconcile every other module gets.

key_symbols.name: configengine.ConfigFile
key_symbols.role: Joins a baseDir and module name into that module's config YAML path; both configsync and the CLI resolve every config path through this one function.

key_symbols.name: yamlengine.Reconcile
key_symbols.role: The actual key-diffing engine: parses template and existing YAML into node trees, computes added/removed leaf key-paths by set difference, overlays existing values onto the template's structure, and remarshals -- this is what configsync.ReconcileAll and ReconcileFabricAt both call to do the real comparison.

key_symbols.name: yamlengine.MissingKeys
key_symbols.role: A read-only sibling of Reconcile used by configengine.Load to detect a config file missing keys its template requires, without merging or writing anything.

key_symbols.name: configcli.runReconcile
key_symbols.role: Handler for the `lyx config reconcile` subcommand -- the primary user-facing entry point -- which resolves the worktree's baseDir and calls configsync.ReconcileAll, then reports each module's added/removed/applied/migratedFrom fields as JSON.

key_symbols.name: fabriccli.CloneAndWire
key_symbols.role: The clone-time entry point: after fabricengine.CloneHub, calls configsync.ReconcileFabricAt for the repo-wide fabric.yaml and then configsync.ReconcileAll for every per-worktree module config, committing whatever each call materializes.

key_symbols.name: fabriccli.runReconcile
key_symbols.role: The `lyx fabric reconcile` handler, which also calls configsync.ReconcileFabricAt before its own fabric-specific reconcile logic runs, since a stale fabric.yaml would otherwise be read by the rest of the command.

summary: The reconciliation mechanism spans four packages plus two CLI entry points. internal/configreg owns the registry: Modules() returns every known module's name, template function, and a SeedOnly flag marking modules whose key set is operator-owned rather than template-derived. internal/yamlengine owns the actual comparison: Reconcile parses a template and an existing file into YAML node trees, computes added and removed leaf key-paths by set difference, overlays existing values onto the template's structure, and remarshals the result; MissingKeys is a read-only sibling used only to detect absence, never to merge. internal/configsync is the orchestration layer sitting between them: ReconcileAll walks configreg.Modules() (skipping the repo-wide fabric module and special-casing SeedOnly modules to materialize-only-when-absent) and calls yamlengine.Reconcile per module, while ReconcileFabricAt handles the one module ReconcileAll skips, additionally folding in values from two pre-cutover config files on first materialization. internal/configengine supplies the shared path-joining (ConfigFile) every one of these packages resolves a config path through, and its own Load/LoadOrTemplate functions call yamlengine.MissingKeys (not Reconcile) to fail or degrade a strict load. Two independent entry points trigger the mechanism: internal/configcli's `lyx config reconcile` command calls ReconcileAll directly, and internal/fabriccli's clone (CloneAndWire) and `fabric reconcile` handlers call both ReconcileFabricAt and ReconcileAll as part of a larger wiring sequence.
open_questions: internal/hubforge/seed.go's SeedConfig/SeedFabricConfig write config files directly and go through configengine.ConfigFile, but they override an already-reconciled file for test fixtures rather than performing reconciliation themselves -- treated as adjacent rather than part of the mechanism proper.

internal/burlerengine/config.go documents that the burler module (SeedOnly) is written verbatim once rather than reconciled key-by-key; confirmed by configreg.go's SeedOnly flag and configsync.go's SeedOnly branch, not by reading burlerengine/config.go's own logic in detail.
